vuln_id: ARVO arvo:56037 / libgit2 smart transport set_data heap-buffer-overflow

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 56037 reports an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ in `set_data`, reachable via `ref_pkt` and `git_pkt_parse_line` while `download_refs_fuzzer` connects to a smart transport.
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is a 65536-byte smart-protocol pkt-line stream, so libgit2's first smart-transport read fills the fixed 64 KiB `gitno_buffer` completely. The stream starts with `000d# comment`, so `git_pkt_parse_line` accepts a 13-byte comment packet and `gitno_consume` shifts the remaining 65523 bytes to the front. In the vulnerable buffer implementation, that consume path zeros from the old `buf->offset` before subtracting the 13 consumed bytes, so after a full-buffer consume the new logical end is not NUL-terminated. The shifted buffer now begins with a ref advertisement whose pkt-line header is `00f2` and whose payload is `40-hex-oid`, a space, `HEAD`, an embedded NUL, and the capability string `multi_ack thin-pack side-band side-band-64k ofs-delta shallo5 deepen-since deepen-not deepen-rflative no-erogress includeKtag multi_ack_detailed synref=HEAD:refs/heads/master agent=git/2.11.0\n`; that capability list omits `object-format=` entirely. Because this is the first ref packet, `ref_pkt` calls `set_data`, which finds the embedded NUL after `HEAD` and then falls through to `strstr(caps, " object-format=")`. Since `caps` is only bounded by the 65523 unread bytes and no longer terminated at the new logical end, that C-string search scans past the remaining pkt-line data and overreads the heap-allocated `transport_smart` object. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 65487 in `set_data` line 234, and the allocation stack points to `git_transport_smart` line 480. The fix replaces `gitno_buffer` consumption with `git_staticstr_consume()`, which restores a terminator at the new logical end so the same capability scan stays within bounds.

source.description: First project-code statement that materializes attacker-controlled pkt-line bytes into libgit2's smart-transport buffer and records the full-buffer state used on the crashing path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 65536 bytes, and `fuzzer_stream_read()` returns `min(buf_size, avail)` with both equal to 65536 on the first callback. This read therefore copies the entire witness into `t->buffer.data` and leaves `buf->offset == buf->len == 65536`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `caps` points into the ref advertisement's capability bytes, but after the stale consume state it is no longer guaranteed to terminate at the buffer's logical end, so this C-string search can run off the heap-backed transport object.
sink.note: The saved vulnerable run reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 65487` at this exact line, with callers `ref_pkt` and `git_pkt_parse_line`, and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 66080-byte region allocated in `git_transport_smart`.

root_cause.description: When a packet is consumed from a full `gitno_buffer`, this sequence shifts the unread tail and shrinks `offset` but never writes a NUL terminator at the new logical end. Later code then treats the remaining pkt-line bytes as an unterminated C string.
root_cause.note: On this witness `buf->offset == buf->len == 65536` and the first parsed packet consumes 13 bytes. `memset` starts at the old end and clears zero bytes, then `buf->offset` becomes 65523, leaving the new logical end stale. The fixing commit removes this bug by using `git_staticstr_consume()`, which re-establishes `data[len] = '\0'` after every consume.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first four bytes of the staged stream are parsed as the first pkt-line length. For this witness ASCII `000d` materializes `len == 13`, which becomes the exact byte count removed from the full transport buffer before the stale-end state is created.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The exact staged `poc` begins with bytes `30 30 30 64` (`"000d"`).

parser_admitted.description: After `git_remote_connect()` selects the RPC upload-pack listing service and step 1 fills the buffer, `git_smart__store_refs` enters pkt-line parsing at this call site.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness exposes the exact 65536-byte witness through a custom smart subtransport and calls `git_remote_connect` in fetch mode.
libgit2 reads the entire witness into its fixed 64 KiB smart-transport buffer in one callback, creating the full-buffer state that the later consume bug mishandles.
The opening `000d# comment` pkt-line is consumed from that full buffer, but the unread tail is shifted left without restoring a NUL terminator at the new logical end.
The shifted buffer front is parsed as the first ref advertisement, so `ref_pkt` invokes `set_data` on its 238-byte `HEAD\0capabilities` payload.

Because the capability bytes omit `object-format=` and the consumed full buffer is no longer terminated at its logical end, `strstr` scans off the heap object and triggers the saved heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source step. The exact staged witness is 65536 bytes, so this callback copies the entire stream into `t->buffer.data` in one read. The buffer now begins `000d# comment00f2...`, and `buf->offset == buf->len == 65536`.
The first four buffered bytes `000d` decode to `len == 13` for the opening pkt-line. That attacker-controlled scalar becomes the number of bytes later removed from the full buffer.

fine_trace.code:
else if (*line == '#')
	error = comment_pkt(pkt, line, len);
fine_trace.note: After the 13-byte length from step 2 is accepted, the first pkt-line payload starts with `#`, so it is classified as a comment packet, not a ref advertisement. No capabilities are parsed here, leaving `data->seen_capabilities == 0` for the next packet.

Root-cause step. With `buf->offset == buf->len == 65536` from step 1 and `consumed == 13` from step 2, `memmove` shifts 65523 unread bytes to the front, `memset` starts at the old end and clears zero bytes, and then `buf->offset` becomes 65523. The new logical end at `buf->data[65523]` is therefore left unterminated.

fine_trace.code: len -= PKT_LEN_SIZE; /* the encoded length includes its own size */
fine_trace.note: At the shifted buffer front, the next pkt-line header is `00f2`, so the parser reduces the total packet length 242 to a 238-byte payload. Because step 3 left `data->seen_capabilities == 0`, this packet is then routed to `ref_pkt`, which calls `set_data` on that first ref advertisement.

Within the 238-byte ref payload from step 5, `memchr` finds the embedded NUL after `HEAD`, so `caps` is advanced to the capability bytes beginning `multi_ack thin-pack ... agent=git/2.11.0\n`. Static inspection of the staged witness shows that substring does not contain `object-format=` anywhere.

Sink step. The capability bytes from step 6 do not match the leading `object-format=` check, so execution falls through to this unbounded `strstr`. Because step 4 left the full-buffer tail unterminated at its new logical end, the search runs past the 65523 unread bytes and crosses the 66080-byte `transport_smart` allocation. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 65487` at this line.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The ASan allocation stack points to the `transport_smart` object that contains `buffer_data`; the trace's root cause explains how stale consume state on that buffer lets `set_data` read past the same allocation.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 saved `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_56037 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 65487` in `set_data` with callers `ref_pkt` and `git_pkt_parse_line`.

format.name: Exact staged 65536-byte git smart-protocol pkt-line stream
format.contract: Verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 65536-byte witness `gt_results/arvo_56037/poc` with SHA-256 `4e12df82a9b2544b0eb5e382a3dd9b14ccee4d1812c5cda4489d2965903cba2b`. Its first pkt-line is ASCII `000d# comment`, so vulnerable libgit2 consumes 13 bytes from a completely full 64 KiB smart-transport buffer. The shifted buffer then begins with pkt-line header `00f2` and a ref advertisement whose payload contains `HEAD\0multi_ack ... agent=git/2.11.0\n` but no `object-format=` capability. On the saved vulnerable run, that exact full-buffer state and capability string make `gitno_consume` leave the post-consume buffer unterminated and make `set_data`'s `strstr` overread the `transport_smart` allocation. This contract does not generalize to smaller reads, other consume lengths, other capability strings, or a broader class of pkt-line inputs.
